subject: Competitive bake-off recap & next steps \u2014 Redwood vs. Competitors
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Rivera <trivera@acmehealth.com>, Lisa Chen <lchen@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Competitive bake-off recap & next steps — Redwood vs. Competitors

Hi Tom / Lisa —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned. Please reply with any corrections.

Summary of pain points you shared:
- High per-token inference cost at peak for summarization pipelines (~$0.XX/token currently)
- Unpredictable 95th pct latency under bursty load (direction: <200ms target)
- Need for deterministic output for regulatory notes (auditability + KMS support)
- Procurement/security checklist items (SOC2 evidence, data residency)

Decision criteria you mentioned:
1) Latency (95th <200ms for summary workload)
2) Cost (total cost of ownership vs current provider)
3) Reliability & fallbacks (SLA/backfill behavior)
4) Security/compliance (SOC2, KMS, VPC option)
5) Ease of integration (SDKs, streaming, model catalog)

What Redwood proposes for the bake-off:
- 2-day performance run (we’ll provide the harness + scripts) covering: throughput/latency at 10/50/100 rps, cold vs warmed KV-cache scenarios
- Accuracy/regression test: run your 1k prompt eval set against Redwood and the other vendors you listed (we’ll accept your ground truth)
- Security/compliance evidence: SOC2 summary + KMS integration guide + sample audit logs

Open questions / items we need from Acme Health:
- Confirm the eval prompt set (roughly 1k prompts) and ground-truth scoring rubric
- Any network/IP allowlist windows we should use for the test cluster
- Procurement timeline and any PO/SOW templates we should use

Attachments:
- redwood-bakeoff-matrix.xlsx (bake-off plan + pass/fail criteria)
- redwood-customer-sow-template.pdf (SOW we can adapt)

Proposed next steps:
1) You confirm evaluation set and a 2-day window (we suggested week of Jun 22)
2) We run the performance test and share raw results and a short write-up
3) We schedule a 1-hour readout + technical Q&A (can include your infra/security team)

Calendly link to book the technical test kickoff: https://calendly.com/aditya-rao/redwood-technical-test

I’ll loop Marissa on pricing and Rishi on the security evidence items.

Thanks — look forward to moving this forward.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Account Exec | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123

--
Attachment: redwood-bakeoff-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)
Attachment: redwood-customer-sow-template.pdf (pdf stub)

From: Tom Rivera <trivera@acmehealth.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lisa Chen <lchen@acmehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Competitive bake-off recap & next steps — Redwood vs. Competitors

Thanks Aditya — this looks good. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Evaluation set: Lisa and I will finalize the 1k prompts by EOD tomorrow and share the scoring rubric.
- Security: we will need SOC2 Type II evidence, encryption-at-rest details, and sample audit logs. Also want to confirm you support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for production.
- Procurement: target decision by end of July. We typically run a 48-hour head-to-head run for each vendor. Can you support back-to-back 48-hour runs for Redwood, CompetitorA, CompetitorB?

For the performance test, we need the harness scripts and the exact test scenarios (rps, payload sizes). Please include an estimate of expected token cost for the 48-hour Redwood run so we can budget.

Also looping our infra lead (cc'd separately if needed) for allowlist and network setup.

On scheduling: the week of Jun 22 works for a kickoff — prefer morning PST. I’ll book a slot on the Calendly link once we finalize time.

Tom
Director of Applied AI | Acme Health
trivera@acmehealth.com | (617) 555-8899

Subject: Re: Competitive bake-off recap & next steps — Redwood vs. Competitors

Tom — thanks for the speedy reply, this is helpful. 

We can absolutely support back-to-back 48-hour runs for each vendor. Proposed plan (high level):
- Day -2: Network allowlist + test harness verification (we provide scripts & container image)
- Day 0-1: Redwood 48-hour run (10/50/100 rps profiles, cold vs warmed cache)
- Day 2-3: CompetitorA 48-hour run (we can help coordinate)
- Day 4-5: CompetitorB 48-hour run

We’ll provide: load scripts, scoring harness, and a raw result dump (latency distributions, request logs, token counts). For budget planning, rough estimate for Redwood run at your throughput/seq lengths is ~$1,200–$1,800 for 48 hours (we’ll provide a precise quote after we see the payload sizes).

Technical deliverables we’ll need from Acme: eval prompt set (1k), allowlist IPs, and a contact for infra to coordinate allowlist windows.

I’ve attached the updated bake-off matrix with pass/fail criteria and a sample SOW.

Marissa — can you prepare a provisional cost estimate and a draft SOW we can hand to procurement? Rishi — can your team assemble the SOC2 + KMS docs and confirm the audit log format we’ll share?

I’ll follow up with a Calendly invite for the kickoff once Tom/Lisa confirm a preferred morning PST slot.

Best,
Aditya
